victim_description: targets in Italy
notes: Google TAG reported that RCS Lab's Hermit spyware was deployed against targets in Italy with the cooperation of Italian authorities and ISPs.

victim_description: targets in Kazakhstan
notes: Google TAG reported Hermit deployments against targets in Kazakhstan, attributed to government use following the January 2022 protests.

victim_description: targets in Syria
notes: Google TAG's February 2024 'Buying Spying' report lists Syria among the countries where RCS Lab's Hermit spyware was deployed; the operating customer is not named in the report.

victim_description: users in Italy, Malaysia and Kazakhstan
notes: Google TAG attributed in-the-wild zero-day exploit chains (Chrome and Firefox) used between 2021 and 2023 to Italy-based Negg Group, with targets observed in Italy, Malaysia and Kazakhstan.

victim_description: targets in Egypt
notes: Google TAG reported Intellexa's Predator spyware campaigns targeting users in Egypt, with delivery via one-click links sent over SMS and WhatsApp.

victim_description: journalists, activists, lawyers and business executives
notes: Meta removed about 40 Facebook and Instagram accounts operated by India-based CyberRoot Risk Advisory for surveillance-for-hire activity, as covered by YourStory citing Meta's December 2022 threat report.

victim_description: Egyptian exiled politician Ayman Nour
notes: Citizen Lab's forensic analysis found Nour's iPhone infected with both Cytrox's Predator and NSO's Pegasus, the first public documentation of a doubly-infected device.

victim_description: 35 journalists and members of civil society in El Salvador, including staff of the newspaper El Faro
notes: Citizen Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus infections across dozens of Salvadoran journalists and activists, one of the most concentrated Pegasus abuses documented.

victim_description: Emirati human rights defender Ahmed Mansoor
notes: Mansoor received exploit-laden text messages that he did not click; Citizen Lab reverse-engineered the iOS exploit chain (Trident) from them and attributed the operation to UAE-linked actors.

victim_description: Saudi dissident Omar Abdulaziz, then resident in Canada
notes: Citizen Lab confirmed a Pegasus infection of Abdulaziz's phone and linked the operators to Saudi Arabia.

victim_description: 36 personal phones belonging to Al Jazeera journalists, producers, anchors and executives
notes: Citizen Lab found the phones compromised via a suspected zero-click iMessage exploit, attributing the operators to Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

victim_description: Egyptian presidential candidate Ahmed Eltantawy
notes: Citizen Lab found Eltantawy's phone targeted with Predator delivered via network injection at the telecom layer, in an operation it attributed to the Egyptian government.

victim_description: 65 Catalans targeted (63 confirmed infected), including elected officials, journalists, activists and lawyers
notes: Citizen Lab's April 2022 report documented one of the largest mercenary-spyware targeting operations to date, covering infections from 2017-2020.

victim_description: At least 4 Catalans infected with Candiru's DevilsTongue spyware, among the 65 targeted
notes: Citizen Lab confirmed DevilsTongue infections alongside Pegasus in the CatalanGate operation, a rare public forensic confirmation of Candiru's spyware in the wild.

victim_description: Moroccan journalist Omar Radi
notes: Amnesty International's Security Lab found Pegasus traces on Radi's phone following network-injection attacks.

victim_description: Carine Kanimba, daughter of detained activist Paul Rusesabagina
notes: Amnesty's Security Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus on Kanimba's phone as part of the Pegasus Project; she was named in partner reporting.

victim_description: Hungarian investigative journalist Szabolcs Panyi (Direkt36)
notes: Amnesty's Security Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus on Panyi's phone as part of the Pegasus Project; he was named in partner reporting.

victim_description: Indian journalist Siddharth Varadarajan, founding editor of The Wire
notes: Amnesty's Security Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus on Varadarajan's phone as part of the Pegasus Project; he was named in partner reporting.

victim_description: Al Jazeera anchorwoman Ghada Oueiss
notes: Amnesty's Security Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus on Oueiss's phone as part of the Pegasus Project; she was named in partner reporting.

victim_description: Azerbaijani investigative journalist Khadija Ismayilova
notes: Amnesty International forensically confirmed Pegasus traces on Ismayilova's phone, as reported in March 2021.

victim_description: French journalist Lenaig Bredoux (Mediapart)
notes: Amnesty's Security Lab forensically confirmed Pegasus on Bredoux's phone as part of the Pegasus Project; she was named in partner reporting.

victim_description: Greek financial journalist Thanasis Koukakis
notes: Amnesty's Predator Files brief documented Koukakis's targeting with Intellexa's Predator in Greece; targeting occurred during 2021 per the case history.

victim_description: Journalists at the US-based Ethiopian Satellite Television (ESAT)
notes: Citizen Lab documented Hacking Team RCS spyware targeting ESAT journalists, attributing the operation to Ethiopian operators.

Amnesty International's Security Lab reported that in summer 2025 the lawyer received a malicious link over WhatsApp from an unknown number; Amnesty attributed the link to a Predator attack attempt based on the technical behaviour of the infection server and one-time-link characteristics consistent with previously observed Predator 1-click links. Amnesty described it as the first reported evidence of Predator use in Pakistan and did not attribute the attack to a specific government; Pakistani officials rejected the report as 'baseless'.
victim_description: an (unnamed) human rights lawyer from Pakistan's Balochistan province

notes: Amnesty International's Security Lab forensically confirmed that Predator spyware was used in 2024 to target Candido's iPhone — the first forensic confirmation of Predator use in Angola. Amnesty recovered Predator-consistent artifacts linked to a 4 May 2024 event and could not attribute the attack to a specific government customer. The case emerged from a broader 2025 investigation by Friends of Angola and Front Line Defenders.
victim_description: Teixeira Candido — prominent Angolan journalist, press freedom activist, jurist and former Secretary General of the Syndicate of Angolan Journalists (SJA), as described by Amnesty International

notes: Amnesty International's Predator Files documented the 1-click campaign sending Predator links to social media accounts. Citizen Lab independently analysed the since-deleted posts (dubbing the actor REPLYSPY) and assessed with 'high confidence' that they contained Cytrox Predator infection links aimed at US and international officials; Google TAG confirmed to Amnesty that the domains and URLs were linked to Intellexa's Predator system. Amnesty reported evidence of Intellexa product sales to Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security and that Google associated the campaign with 'a government actor in Vietnam'.
victim_description: US senators and representatives, the President of Taiwan, UN officials, European Parliament and European Commission political figures, academics, think-tanks and a Berlin-based news website — targeted (not necessarily infected) via Predator infection links posted in replies from the X account @Joseph_Gordon16

notes: Meta reported in its Adversarial Threat Report for Q4 2023 (published February 2024) that a network of fictitious personas linked to RCS Labs — which Meta described as owned by Cy4Gate — tricked users into sharing contact details and clicking bogus reconnaissance links.
victim_description: social media users in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Mongolia targeted by RCS Labs-linked fictitious personas impersonating activists, journalists and young women to harvest phone numbers, email addresses and contact details and deliver reconnaissance links

notes: Meta reported that removed Facebook and Instagram accounts associated with Spanish spyware vendor Variston IT were employed for exploit development and testing, including sharing of malicious links; Meta also reported the company was discontinuing operations.
victim_description: Facebook and Instagram users exposed to Variston IT's exploit-development and spyware-delivery testing via malicious links (accounts removed by Meta)

notes: Meta reported in its Adversarial Threat Report for Q4 2023 (published February 2024) that Italy-based Negg Group used social media accounts to test delivery of its spyware.
victim_description: social media users exposed to Negg Group's spyware delivery testing via malicious links (accounts removed by Meta)

notes: Meta reported in its Adversarial Threat Report for Q4 2023 (published February 2024) that Spain-based Mollitiam Industries used social media accounts to test delivery of its spyware.
victim_description: social media users exposed to Mollitiam Industries' spyware delivery testing via malicious links (accounts removed by Meta)
